E6.name: E6
E6.title: Svinesund – Oslo – Trondheim – Kirkenes
E6.role: Norway's backbone: Svinesund (Swedish border) – Oslo – Hamar – Lillehammer – Dovrefjell – Trondheim – Mo i Rana – Narvik – Alta – Kirkenes.
E6.freight: Most road freight to and from Europe crosses the border at Svinesund on the E6, including fresh salmon heading south. North of Trondheim it is the only through road, so a closure on Dovrefjell or Saltfjellet cuts the country in two for trucks.

E18.name: E18
E18.title: Ørje – Oslo – Kristiansand
E18.role: Ørje (Swedish border) – Oslo – Drammen – Porsgrunn – Arendal – Kristiansand along the south coast.
E18.freight: Links Oslo with the south coast ports (Larvik, Kristiansand) and with Stockholm via Ørje. Very heavy traffic around Oslo and Drammen.

E39.name: E39
E39.title: Kristiansand – Stavanger – Bergen – Trondheim
E39.role: The coastal road Kristiansand – Stavanger – Bergen – Førde – Ålesund – Molde – Trondheim.
E39.freight: Bergen's link to Stavanger and the north. Several ferry crossings make trips slow and costly per kilometre; Rogfast (a subsea tunnel under construction) will replace the ferry north of Stavanger, and the plan is to remove more ferries over time.

E16.name: E16
E16.title: Bergen – Lærdal – Oslo – Sweden
E16.role: Bergen – Voss – Lærdal – Filefjell – Valdres – Hønefoss – Oslo – Kongsvinger – Sweden.
E16.freight: The main year-round truck route between Bergen and Oslo, because Filefjell is lower and closes less often than Haukelifjell and Hardangervidda. It includes Lærdalstunnelen, 24.5 km long. East of Oslo it carries timber and goods to and from Sweden.

E134.name: E134
E134.title: Drammen – Haukeli – Haugesund
E134.freight: The southern east–west route between Oslo and the west coast, and the main road for Haugesund and Sunnhordland. Haukelifjell runs convoys or closes in winter storms, which sends trucks over to the E16.

E136.name: E136
E136.title: Dombås – Ålesund
E136.freight: Connects Møre's industry, shipyards and seafood exporters with the E6.

E10.name: E10
E10.title: Lofoten – Narvik – Sweden
E10.role: Å in Lofoten – Svolvær – Narvik – Bjørnfjell (Swedish border) – Kiruna.
E10.freight: Lofoten's seafood road and Narvik's link to Sweden. The Ofoten ore railway runs alongside it to Narvik port.

E8.name: E8
E8.title: Tromsø – Finland
E8.freight: Tromsø's route to Finland. Much seafood from Troms goes this way by truck to Finland and on to Europe.

E14.name: E14
E14.title: Trondheim – Sweden
E14.freight: Trondheim's road to Sweden, Östersund and Sundsvall.

Rv7.name: Rv7
Rv7.title: Hønefoss – Hardangervidda – Granvin
Rv7.role: Hønefoss – Gol – Geilo – Hardangervidda – Eidfjord – Granvin.
Rv7.freight: The shortest road between Oslo and Bergen in summer, but the crossing of Hardangervidda often closes or runs convoys in winter, so many trucks choose the E16.

Rv52.name: Rv52
Rv52.title: Gol – Hemsedalsfjellet – Borlaug
Rv52.freight: A shortcut between Hallingdal and Lærdal used by trucks between Oslo and Western Norway; a mountain pass exposed to winter closures.

Rv2.name: Rv2
Rv2.title: Kongsvinger – Elverum
Rv2.freight: Links the forest districts of Innlandet with the E16 and Sweden.

Rv3.name: Rv3
Rv3.title: Østerdalen: Elverum – Ulsberg
Rv3.freight: The trucks' alternative to the E6 between Oslo and Trondheim, avoiding Dovrefjell. It has one of the highest shares of heavy vehicles of any main road.

Rv4.name: Rv4
Rv4.title: Oslo – Gjøvik
Rv4.freight: Oslo's road north on the west side of Mjøsa.

Rv5.name: Rv5
Rv5.title: Florø – Førde – Lærdal
Rv5.freight: Sunnfjord's link to the E16 and Eastern Norway.

Rv9.name: Rv9
Rv9.title: Kristiansand – Setesdal – Haukeli
Rv9.freight: Kristiansand's road north to the E134.

Rv13.name: Rv13
Rv13.title: Ryfylke – Hardanger – Vik
Rv13.freight: Fjord and ferry road through Ryfylke and Hardanger; slow, but it serves industry in Odda and fish farming.

Rv15.name: Rv15
Rv15.title: Otta – Strynefjellet – Måløy
Rv15.freight: Seafood from Nordfjord and Måløy to the E6. Strynefjellet is exposed in winter.

pois.name: Haukelifjell
pois.text: High mountain pass on the E134. In winter storms it runs convoys (kolonnekjøring) or closes, sometimes for days.

pois.name: Hardangervidda
pois.text: Long crossing of the plateau on Rv7. Frequently closed or convoy-only in winter, so trucks usually choose the E16.

pois.name: Filefjell
pois.text: The E16 crossing between Valdres and Lærdal. Lower and more sheltered than the alternatives, which is why it is the main winter truck route Bergen–Oslo.

pois.name: Hemsedalsfjellet
pois.text: Rv52 between Hemsedal and Borlaug. Exposed to winter closures.

pois.name: Dovrefjell
pois.text: The E6 over Dovre between Dombås and Oppdal. A closure here sends trucks between Oslo and Trondheim over Rv3 in Østerdalen.

pois.name: Saltfjellet
pois.text: The E6 across the Arctic Circle. There is no alternative road through Norway, so closures stop north–south truck traffic or force detours through Sweden.

pois.name: Strynefjellet
pois.text: Rv15 between Stryn and Grotli. Exposed in winter.

pois.name: Mortavika–Arsvågen
pois.text: The E39 ferry north of Stavanger. Rogfast, a subsea tunnel under construction, will replace it.

pois.name: Halhjem–Sandvikvåg
pois.text: The E39 ferry south of Bergen across Bjørnafjorden. Hordfast is the planned fixed link.

pois.name: Oppedal–Lavik
pois.text: The E39 crossing of Sognefjorden.

pois.name: Anda–Lote
pois.text: The E39 crossing of Nordfjord.

pois.name: Festøya–Solavågen
pois.text: The E39 ferry south of Ålesund.

pois.name: Molde–Vestnes
pois.text: The E39 crossing of Romsdalsfjorden.

pois.name: Halsa–Kanestraum
pois.text: The E39 ferry between Nordmøre and Trøndelag.

pois.name: Svinesund
pois.text: Norway's busiest road border crossing and its main customs post for trucks to and from Europe. Goods must be declared in advance (Digitoll).

pois.name: Ørje
pois.text: E18 border crossing towards Karlstad and Stockholm.

pois.name: Magnor
pois.text: E16 border crossing east of Kongsvinger.

pois.name: Storlien
pois.text: E14 border crossing from Trøndelag to Sweden.

pois.name: Bjørnfjell
pois.text: E10 border crossing between Narvik and Kiruna.

pois.name: Kilpisjärvi
pois.text: E8 border crossing to Finland.

pois.name: Alnabru (Oslo)
pois.text: Norway's largest rail freight terminal, where containers and trailers move between train and truck.

pois.name: Bergen
pois.text: Port and logistics hub; supply base at CCB Ågotnes and the oil terminal at Mongstad to the north.

pois.name: Stavanger (Risavika)
pois.text: Port and offshore supply hub for the oil industry.

pois.name: Trondheim
pois.text: Gateway between southern and northern Norway; rail to the north (Nordlandsbanen) starts here.

pois.name: Kristiansand
pois.text: Ferry port to Denmark and the Netherlands for trailers and cars.

pois.name: Narvik
pois.text: Ore port and rail link to Sweden; a hub for freight to northern Norway.

pois.name: Ålesund
pois.text: Seafood exports and maritime industry.
